gold_assessment.reasoning: Gold states vomiting started 3 days ago. Generated facts only state diarrhea for three days and vomiting initially x2, resolved; they do not specify that vomiting began 3 days ago.
Gold: diarrhea now, 5–6 times/day. Gen hpi-003: watery diarrhea about 5–6 times/day. Matches frequency and current presence of diarrhea.
Gold: watery/loose stools. Gen hpi-003: watery diarrhea; ROS-001: watery diarrhea. The watery/loose nature of stools is captured.
Gold: no blood in stools, no abdominal pain. Gen hpi-004 and ros-005: no blood in stool; hpi-005 and ros-007: no significant abdominal pain. Equivalent content.

Gold: reduced oral intake, not drinking sufficient fluids, feels dehydrated. Gen hpi-006: feels dehydrated and weak; hpi-007: unable to drink sufficient fluids. Reduced oral intake and insufficient fluids with dehydration are represented.
Gold: appetite is reduced. Gen hpi-008 and ros-009: appetite reduced/decreased. Direct match.

Gold: no fever but feels warm and weak (warm currently implied). Gen hpi-009: no fever currently; hpi-006: feels dehydrated and weak. However, gen hpi-010 states felt warm at the start, not currently, which differs from simply ‘feels warm’. Thus, absence of fever and weakness are covered; the warmth description is altered in time course.
Gold: no headaches or muscle pain. Gen hpi-011: no headaches or muscle pains. Fully captured.
Gold: unaware of triggers and no contact with other unwell people. Gen hpi-013: no clear trigger identified; hpi-015: no exposure to others with diarrhea. These correspond to the gold content.
Gold: history of asthma. Gen pmh-001: history of asthma. Direct match.

Gold: salbutamol inhaler PRN. Gen med-001: inhaled blue short-acting inhaler, dose/route/frequency not documented. This implies a SABA inhaler but does not explicitly state PRN usage or the drug name salbutamol, so the fact is only partially represented.
Gold: no known drug allergies. Gen allergy-001: patient denies any known drug allergies. Same information.

Gold: father had hypertension and died of bowel cancer. Gen fh-001: father had hypertension; fh-002: father died of bowel cancer ~10 years ago. Hypertension and bowel cancer death are covered, but the gold fact did not specify timing of death; the 10-year detail is an added element, so the core content is covered.
Gold: mother has Type 2 diabetes. Gen fh-003: mother has diabetes (type 2). Direct match.
Gold: lives alone and works as a software engineer. Gen sh-001: lives alone; sh-002: employed as software engineer. Both components present.
Gold: non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. Gen sh-003: does not smoke; sh-004: drinks alcohol infrequently and socially. Matches with slight, non-contradictory added detail (infrequently).

Gold: impression is gastroenteritis. Gen asm-001: acute gastroenteritis (diarrhea-dominant) with dehydration risk. Acute nature, diarrhea-dominant, and dehydration risk are additional qualifiers; underlying diagnosis gastroenteritis is covered.

Gold: supportive management including rest and increased fluid intake. Gen plan-006: advised to rest and avoid work until symptoms improve; plan-005: emphasize increasing oral fluid intake. Supportive management, rest, and fluids are covered, but plan-001 in gen set is about diagnostics and not this fact, so coverage comes from other plan items.

Gold: recommended OTC oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte). Gen plan-002: Dioralyte oral rehydration solution prescribed to aid fluid and electrolyte replenishment. Same intervention, with extra detail on purpose and ‘prescribed’ vs ‘recommended’ but not contradictory.

Gold: recommended regular paracetamol. Gen plan-003: paracetamol as needed for fever/weakness. Drug is matched, but ‘regular’ versus ‘as needed’ differ; frequency/regimen conflicts, so coverage is partial at best (medication same, regimen inconsistent).
Gold: review in 7 days if not better. Gen fu-001: if not improved by next week, return for re-evaluation. ‘Next week’ aligns with about 7 days and same conditional follow-up.

Gold: seek earlier review if worsening symptoms (diarrhea, vomiting, abdo pain, reduced oral intake). Gen plan-004 and plan-005 mention re-evaluation/return if symptoms persist or worsen. These capture the concept of earlier review for worsening symptoms but do not list the specific symptom examples, and gen fu-002 is about work abstinence, not clinical review. Thus only partially covered.

gen_assessment.reasoning: Chief complaint and explicit 3-day diarrhea duration are not specified in the gold facts (which say vomiting started 3 days ago, not diarrhea).

Gold does not provide age, sex, or specify ‘acute diarrhea for ~3 days’. Only vomiting timing (3 days) and presence of diarrhea are in gold; the 3-day diarrhea duration and demographics are additional.
Gold states vomiting developed 3 days ago but does not mention ‘two episodes’ or that vomiting has resolved. Episode count and resolution status are additional.
Feeling dehydrated is supported by gold hpi-005. Feeling weak is supported by gold hpi-007. Combining both in one fact is acceptable but spans multiple gold facts.
Gold hpi-007: ‘feels warm’ (present sense). Generated hpi-010: ‘felt warm at the start of illness’, implying past warmth only. This alters the temporal status of the warmth symptom.
Symptom onset location (‘at home’) is not mentioned in any gold fact.
No recent travel is not addressed in gold facts.
Gold: no contact with other unwell people (broad). Gen: no exposure to others with diarrhea (specific to diarrhea). This narrows the scope but does not contradict; partially supported.

Gold: salbutamol PRN. Gen: ‘inhaled blue short-acting inhaler’ with dose/route/frequency not documented. Drug class and route align, but the PRN aspect and explicit name ‘salbutamol’ are missing; no contradiction, but incomplete.
Gold does not state whether other medications are taken or not; ‘no other medications’ is new information.
Gold: father died of bowel cancer, no timing. Gen adds ‘~10 years ago’. Diagnosis of bowel cancer death is supported; timing is an additional detail.
Gold: drinks alcohol socially. Gen: drinks alcohol infrequently and socially. Social drinking is supported; ‘infrequently’ is added detail.
Gold describes reduced intake, insufficient fluids, and feeling dehydrated but does not label them as ‘dehydration symptoms’ in ROS; content aligns but section/phrasing is additional.
Gold describes vomiting history but not explicitly in ROS as ‘positive for previous vomiting’. The ROS framing is additional structure, not contradicted.
Gold does not enumerate ‘other systemic symptoms’ in ROS; this negative ROS summary is additional.
Gold: impression is gastroenteritis. Gen: acute gastroenteritis, diarrhea-dominant, with dehydration risk. Diagnosis is supported; acuity, dominance, and risk are added qualifiers.
Gold plan does not mention diagnostics at all. Statement that no labs/imaging were ordered is new information.
Gold: ‘regular paracetamol’ (implying scheduled dosing). Gen: paracetamol ‘as needed’ for fever/weakness. PRN vs regular is a direct regimen discrepancy.

Gold fu-002: earlier review if worsening symptoms; gen plan-004: monitor hydration and consider re-evaluation if symptoms persist or worsen. Concept of re-evaluation on worsening/persistence is supported, though location in Plan vs Follow-up and some phrasing are additional.

Increasing oral fluid intake and rest/self-care align with gold supportive management. Use Dioralyte is supported by gold plan-002. ‘Consider paracetamol’ conflicts with gold ‘regular paracetamol’ regimen, and ‘return if symptoms worsen or fail to improve’ overlaps with gold fu-001 and fu-002 but adds broader phrasing. Mixed supported and additional/contradictory elements.
Advised to rest and avoid work until symptoms improve: rest is consistent with supportive management. Work-avoidance disposition is not mentioned in gold, so that part is additional.
Gold fu-002 is about earlier clinical review for worsening symptoms. Gen fu-002 is about abstaining from work until diarrhea-free 24–48 hours; work restriction is not mentioned in gold.
